title: Coroner's inquest announced into 2015 Vancouver police shooting death
subtitle: Public inquiry will look into the shooting death of Abdi Gani Mahamud Hirsi in the Downtown Eastside in 2015.
article: The B.C. Coroners Service will hold a public inquest into the 2015 police shooting death of 26-year-old Abdi Gani Mahamud Hirsi in Vancouver's Downtown Eastside.
Hirsi was shot dead on April 9, 2015, when he was confronted by VPD officers after he stabbed two men in front of the First United Church at East Hastings Street and Gore Avenue, police say.
The look into Hirsi's death is slated for Nov. 5, 2018, at the Burnaby Coroners' Court, the Ministry of Public Safety and Solicitor General announced Monday.

Coroner Michael Egilson and jurors will hear evidence from witnesses under oath to determine precisely what happened, according to the ministry. The jury can make recommendations on preventing similar future deaths but it cannot make a finding of legal responsibility. Public inquiries are mandatory when someone dies in policy custody, according to the ministry.

Police say they initially shot Hirsi with a beanbag shotgun, but officers then used bullets after he turned his knife on a woman who was standing nearby. Three people were wounded in the incident.

Hirsi had recently come to the city from Alberta to look for work, family members said shortly after his death. They said they did not know what he was doing in the Downtown Eastside in the lead-up to the shooting.
Members of Hirsi's family could not be reached Monday.
